references.text: The prose parallel account of Jael's killing of Sisera, where she drives the tent peg through his temple while he lies sleeping
Describes how Barak finds Sisera lying dead with the tent peg through his head, the same event poetically described in Judges 5:27
Uses similar language about enemies falling and lying scattered—the judgment upon God's enemies
God crushes the heads of His enemies, thematically parallel to Jael's victory over Sisera
The immediate context describing Jael's action with the tent peg and hammer against Sisera
